topics.title: JavaScript values
topics.summary: Compute a value in dekit.yaml with !js, and share values between them with vars.

inlines.text: is a JavaScript expression. dekit evaluates it when it loads the config, and its value takes the tag's place, as if it were written there.

blocks.text:
vars:
  data: !js std.path.join(ctx.runner.root, ".data")
tasks:
  db:
    cmd: !js '["postgres", "-D", ctx.vars.data + "/db"]'
  api:
    cmd: cargo run -p api
    env:
      FIXTURES: !js std.path.join(ctx.dir, "fixtures")
      DATA_DIR: !js ctx.vars.data

Add a task at the path `target` and, unless `start` is false, start it. `spec` is a task entry as in |config/tasks|, with `defaults` under it but for `autorestart`. `place` lists it: `first`, `last`, or `{after: <path>}`; last unless it says.
Redefine the task at `target` in place; `spec` is its whole entry. It runs the new definition from its next start, or now with `restart: true` if it is running.

fields.desc: Tasks by path (|config/tasks|). Paths may nest, as in `services/web`. A key that ends in `/` is a folder (|config/tasks#folders|).
Task settings shared by every task, such as `cwd`, `env`, `autorestart`, or `stop`. A task's own value wins. Not `type` or `ready`.
Values for `!js` to read as `ctx.vars`, in order (|config/js#vars|).
More files with tasks, as globs (|config/load|).
The dekit binary that runs this project (|config/kernel|).
The runner's own debug log. `level` is off, error, warn, info, debug, or trace.
A command to run once the project has loaded (|config/hooks|).
A command to run each time the last active task goes idle (|config/hooks|).
The program to run and its arguments. An array is the exact argv; a string is split into words (|config/tasks#commands|).
A `.js` or `.mjs` file to run on dekit's built-in JavaScript runtime (|js|).
The name shown in the TUI. Defaults to the task path.
A service keeps running; a job runs to completion (|config/tasks#jobs|).
Tasks that must be ready, or done for a job, before this one starts, each by its path. Starting this task starts them too.
Tags for `+tag` targets (|start/targets|). Two are the runner's to give, `autostart` from the setting below, and `dynamic`, which every task not from the config has and the config refuses.
When the task counts as ready, so its dependents can start (|config/tasks#ready|). Without it, the task is ready once it starts.
Working directory. Defaults to the project root.
Extra environment variables. A null value removes the variable.
Directories to put in front of PATH.
Start the task on `dekit up`; a runner that starts on its own starts no task. It adds the `autostart` tag.
When to start the task again by itself after it exits (|config/tasks#restarting|).
How to stop the task, as a signal name or an object (|config/tasks#stopping|).
Also write the task's output to a file (|config/tasks#logs|).
Lines of output kept for scrolling back.
Lines per mouse-wheel step in the TUI.
The TUI lists the folder collapsed the first time it shows it. After that the folder stays as you leave it, across restarts too.

The program reports it, as it would to systemd, by sending `READY=1` to the Unix datagram socket named by `NOTIFY_SOCKET` in its environment. The socket is dekit's and outlives restarts; the rest of the protocol is ignored. Not on Windows.
How long to wait between tries of `tcp`, `http`, `cmd`, and `file`. A try that takes longer than this (at least 1s) counts as failed.
If the task is not ready this long after it started, the start failed. dekit stops the task, and `autorestart` decides whether it runs again. No limit by default.
